clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of photosensitive erythematous macules and papules, which on examination were sharply demarcated erythematous plaques. Serological tests revealed positive Antinuclear factor (1:320) and elevated anti-dsDNA (38.9 IU/mL), indicating Systemic Lupus Erythematosus. Urinalysis showed proteinuria 2+, massive hematuria, and elevated white blood cells, suggesting renal involvement. A kidney biopsy was performed, which showed focal crescentic and focal mesangial type of glomerular damage with full-blown positivity of IgA, IgG, and C1q immunohistochemically. These findings were explicitly classified as lupus nephritis class III-A according to the ISN/RPS 2003 classification.

Urinalysis indicated kidney involvement with proteinuria 2+, massive hematuria, and a white blood cell count of 32/µL.
Kidney biopsy histopathology showed focal crescentic and focal mesangial type of glomerular damage with full-blown positivity of IgA, IgG, and C1q.
The kidney biopsy findings were classified as lupus nephritis class III-A according to the ISN/RPS 2003 classification.
